beats.say: Now messages: SMS, WhatsApp and Telegram. Scammers pose as a courier, a prize or someone close.
Courier texts with a tiny fee are common. The link opens a fake page that steals card details.

messages.text: Your parcel is held at the depot, the address is incomplete.

checkpoint.prompt: A courier text asks for a 1.20 AZN fee. What do you do?

options.label: I pay via the link, it is a small sum
options.feedback: The small sum is bait: the page steals card details.

options.label: I check the parcel in the courier's official app
options.feedback: Right. Open the official app yourself, not the link in the text.

beats.say: The most dangerous is a code request. With it, they move your account to their phone.

body.text: Hi, I typed your number by mistake. You will get a 6 digit code, can you send it to me?

beats.say: Protection is simple: never send the code, and turn on two step verification in your messenger.

scenes.title: New number
scenes.intro: In the evening, a WhatsApp message arrives from an unknown number. The sender says she is your daughter.

body.text: Hi Mum! It's me, Aysel. My phone broke, this is my new number.

steps.say: The number is new, the name is familiar.

actions.label: Hi, sweetheart! What happened?
actions.feedback: Nothing is lost yet, but this is exactly how the scam starts. Check the old number first.

actions.label: Call Aysel's old number
actions.feedback: Great check. Always confirm a new number using a familiar name through another channel.

body.text: I urgently need 300 manat, send it to this card. I will pay you back tomorrow.
I can't call, the microphone is broken.

actions.label: I send the money
actions.feedback: The money went to the scammer's card. The 'cannot call' excuse is there to stop you checking.

actions.label: I ask something only she would know
actions.feedback: A good check. But the surest way is to call the old number yourself.

actions.label: I call her old number
actions.feedback: Right. Check a new number asking for money through the old, familiar one.

body.text: Also, a six-digit code is coming to you, send it to me. I am moving WhatsApp to my new phone.

actions.label: I send the code
actions.feedback: This code opens your own account. Whoever gets it takes over your WhatsApp and writes as you.

actions.label: I give the code to no one
actions.feedback: Right. Never give a verification code to anyone, not even family.

actions.label: Block and report
actions.feedback: Great. Block a new number that asks for a code, then call the old number.

body.text: Mum, my phone is fine, I have not written to anyone! It is a scam.

steps.say: This is Aysel's old, familiar number.

actions.label: Warn everyone in the family group
actions.feedback: Right. The scammer will send the same story to your relatives.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The fake number is still active. Block it and warn your family.

scenes.prompt: Find the traps in this message.

spots.label: A number you do not know
spots.explain: Prize draws are not announced from a private number. But even a familiar name can be faked.

spots.label: A prize in a draw you never entered
spots.explain: You cannot win a contest you never entered.

spots.label: Time pressure
spots.explain: A short deadline is there to make you act without thinking.

spots.label: A fee for a prize
spots.explain: The small fee is an excuse to get your card details.

spots.label: Unknown link
spots.explain: This address belongs to no known organisation. Do not tap links like this.

messages.text: We could not deliver your parcel. Update your address:

cards.explain: The link does not lead to the courier's own site. Check the tracking number on the official site yourself.

messages.text: Code: 551920. It confirms your online payment. Do not share this code with anyone.

cards.explain: A normal code text that arrives when you pay online yourself. No link, and it reminds you not to share.

body.text: Hi! A code went to your number by mistake, please send it to me.

cards.explain: This is an account takeover. The code would move your account to their phone.

body.text: Tomorrow's meeting moved to 11, same room.

cards.explain: No link, no code, no request for money. A normal work message.

body.text: Hi, it is me, my phone broke and this is my new number. Send 250 manat to my card, it is urgent.

cards.explain: A new number and an urgent request for money. Call your relative on their old number to check.

messages.text: Your application has been received. You can see the result in your personal account on the official portal.

cards.explain: It asks for no link click or payment. You open the portal yourself from the address you know.

question.prompt: A friend on WhatsApp asks for the code you received. What do you do?

options.label: I send it, they are my friend
options.feedback: Your friend's account may already be stolen. The code would hand them your account too.

options.label: I do not send it and call my friend to warn them
options.feedback: Correct. Often the friend's account has been taken over and the scammer writes in their name.

options.label: I ignore it and forget about it
options.feedback: Good that you kept the code. But warn your friend, their account may be stolen.

scenes.explain: This is how takeovers spread: a stolen account asks friends for codes. A code is never sent to anyone.

points: Do not tap courier or prize links
Check a new number asking for money by calling the old one
Never send a code, turn on two step verification
